Method of Attack: Uploading malicious packages to PyPI resembling popular open-source tools to trick developers
Using a fake Python package mirror (typosquatting) to host poisoned versions of legitimate packages
Hijacking privileged GitHub accounts to alter project files to point to malicious dependencies
Malicious Python code downloads a loader/dropper script that fetches encrypted final payload
Establishing persistence by modifying Windows Registry
Stealing browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, Telegram session data, Instagram session tokens, keystrokes, and files from user directories
Uploading stolen data to attacker-controlled servers and anonymous file-sharing services
Impacted Systems: Windows systems compromised by the malware
Browsers: Opera, Chrome, Brave, Vivaldi, Yandex, Edge
Attack Vector: Hijacked GitHub maintainer account (editor-syntax) committing malicious code
Malicious dependencies in requirements.txt pointing to poisoned packages
Indicators of Compromise: Fake Python package mirror URL: files.pypihosted.org
Malicious package names: yocolor, altered colorama
Malicious commits in Top.gg python-sdk repository
Use of anonymous file-sharing services: GoFile, Anonfiles
HTTP requests with unique hardware ID and IP address identifiers
